name: DiveSchedule
description: Dive-operations system for commercial hull-cleaning outfits: recurring boat rotations, a checklist-and-certify workflow with an immutable service record per cleaning, crew pay, point-of-sale against inventory, and an income/expense ledger.

permissions.description: See every scheduled cleaning job on the board, for every boat and diver.
See only the jobs this diver is assigned to.
Create, edit, reschedule, assign and delete cleaning jobs and their rotations.
Work a job: run the checklist, attach proof photos and video, and certify it complete.
See the price and estimate figures on a job (hidden from divers who only work them).
Edit the shop's cleaning checklist template that every job is worked against.
See the immutable service record produced by each completed cleaning.
Send a completed service record to the boat owner.
See the diver roster, certifications and contact details.
Add and edit diver profiles, certifications and pay rates.
See this diver's own weekly earnings breakdown.
See weekly pay for the whole crew.
Run the point of sale: take cash payment against inventory and record the sale.
See revenue, the income/expense ledger and the trend report.
See parts, tools and stock levels.
Add, edit, delete and restock inventory items.
Change app settings: rates, templates and thresholds.

scopes.purpose: Read the dive operation's display name and timezone for service-record headers and for the weekly pay-period boundaries.
Resolve divers to platform users for job assignment, completed-by attribution on service records, and weekly pay reporting.
Gate every job, record, pay, POS, finance and inventory action server-side against the signed-in user's effective plugin permissions (e.g. a diver sees only assigned jobs and their own pay).
Drive suspended/past-due UX from real platform subscription state instead of a local gate.

$comment_webhooks: installation.deleted drives the full per-installation cascade delete (the 30-day deletion obligation, contract §11). The subscription events are received and logged today; the entitlement UX that consumes them is not built yet.
$comment_sensitiveScopes: Empty on purpose. Contract §9 makes an independent penetration test a GATE on the first production grant of any sensitive-tier scope, pilots included. Nothing here needs PII-populated users/tenant today: divers are resolved by platform user id, and service records carry the boat, not the owner's personal data. Do not add an entry without booking that pen test first.
